questions.q: Does PostgreSQL's basic WITH CTE syntax differ from the standard syntax covered in Chapter 4?
options: No — the basic WITH name AS (...) syntax is unchanged; this lesson covers behavior around it, not new syntax
Yes — PostgreSQL requires a different keyword entirely for non-recursive CTEs
Yes — PostgreSQL requires every CTE to specify a column list
Yes — PostgreSQL CTEs cannot be joined to other tables
questions.explain: The syntax itself carries over from Chapter 4; what's PostgreSQL-specific is the materialization behavior and recursion keyword.

questions.q: What was PostgreSQL's CTE 'optimization fence' behavior before version 12?
options: CTEs were always inlined and never materialized
CTEs could not be used in a WHERE clause at all
Every CTE was always fully materialized (run and stored) rather than inlined into the outer query
CTEs automatically converted themselves into temporary tables on disk
questions.explain: Pre-12 PostgreSQL always materialized CTEs, which could make them noticeably slower than an equivalent subquery even with identical SQL text.

questions.q: What changed about CTE behavior starting in PostgreSQL 12?
options: CTEs were removed entirely in favor of subqueries
Non-recursive CTEs are inlined into the outer query by default, unless explicitly marked MATERIALIZED
MATERIALIZED became the mandatory default with no way to opt out
Recursive CTEs became inlined by default instead of materialized
questions.explain: PostgreSQL 12 flipped the default so non-recursive CTEs behave more like subqueries unless you explicitly request the old fenced behavior.

questions.q: What keyword does PostgreSQL require for a self-referencing (recursive) CTE that T-SQL and Oracle do not require?
options: ITERATE, as in WITH ITERATE
LOOP, as in WITH LOOP
SELF, as in WITH SELF
RECURSIVE, as in WITH RECURSIVE
questions.explain: PostgreSQL requires WITH RECURSIVE explicitly — the same requirement MySQL has, but different from T-SQL and Oracle, which infer recursion automatically.

questions.q: Why would you explicitly add MATERIALIZED to a CTE on PostgreSQL 12 or later?
options: To convert the CTE into a permanent table
To make the CTE run faster in all cases, with no tradeoffs
Because MATERIALIZED is now required syntax for every CTE
To force the pre-12 fenced behavior, e.g. when the CTE has a side effect or you want to stabilize the query plan
questions.explain: MATERIALIZED is an opt-in override for cases where you specifically want the older always-materialized behavior back.
